name: coherent population shrink: every epoch cut to its first 120 rounds, every self-reported count doctored to agree, dataset re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 12. Step 12 (Dataset Integrity & Population Identity) must reject a dataset that is not the audited population (G-BIND): the rounds with nonce 120 and above are deleted from every epoch, and the header totals, the per-phase counts, the per-run counts, each seed record's plannedBets and nonceEnd are all set to agree, so every count INSIDE the file is coherent. The expected population comes from EXPECTED_BETS, EXPECTED_SEEDS and CAPTURE_PLAN in src/config.ts, so the step fails; Step 4 fails with it. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: pre-commitment chain severed: run 1's pre-capture record no longer names its first commitment
guard: The guard that fires is Step 2. Step 2 (Next-Seed Pre-Commitment Chain) must reject a run whose first link is missing: the transitions inside a run say nothing about the run's first commitment, which would otherwise be simply the first thing the auditor saw. What places it earlier is the run's pre-capture pair, whose nextHashedServerSeed must BE that commitment. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: pre-capture reveal forged: the seed released before run 1's first bet no longer hashes to its own commitment
guard: The guard that fires is Step 2. Step 2 (Next-Seed Pre-Commitment Chain) must verify the pre-capture record as a commitment in its own right, not merely as a pointer: an anchor whose own revealed seed does not hash to its commitment is unverifiable. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: pre-commitment chain severed on the 10 November run: run 2's pre-capture record no longer names its first commitment
guard: The guard that fires is Step 2. Step 2 (Next-Seed Pre-Commitment Chain) must anchor EVERY run, not only the first: the three runs are separate sessions, so each run's first commitment needs its own pre-capture link. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: bet settled against a commitment no seed record backs

The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: nonce window doctored: a seed record's recorded end moved under a full epoch

name: win flag flipped: a losing round relabelled a win
guard: The guard that fires is Step 6. Step 6 (Win-Rule Reproduction) must derive the win flag from the RECOMPUTED result and the chosen target, not read it: bet 9woTGRttiUxaK2tF7nmig (epoch 0, nonce 6) produced 1.21x against a 1.77x target; relabelling it a win contradicts the recomputation. Steps 9 and 20 fail as well, because a win with a zero credit is also an arithmetic contradiction. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: paid multiplier forged: a win served at a rate the player did not choose
guard: The guard that fires is Step 8. Step 8 (Paid-Multiplier Derivation) must assert the served multiplier IS the chosen target, bit-exact. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: credit forged by one unit in the eighth decimal place, on the game field and the wallet field

Step 9 (Credit Arithmetic) must reject a credit that is not the EXACT decimal product of stake and target: bet 3G5Wm6eniZ8jXrzab4IJd is 0.10 at 1.01x, credited 0.10100000; the forgery credits 0.10100001. The wallet field is moved in the same edit so Step 11's cross-check cannot be what catches it; Step 20 fails alongside. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: loss relabelled 'won' while crediting nothing

The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: two records carrying one settlement id
guard: The guard that fires is Step 12. Step 12 (Dataset Integrity & Population Identity) must require 5,838 DISTINCT settlement ids: a row count is not an identity. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: bet moved between phases: a 0.10 Phase A round relabelled Phase C

Step 13 (Phase Plan Conformance) must check the plan in both directions: the move breaks the Phase A and Phase C counts, puts a 0.10 stake and a 1.01x target into Phase C, and disagrees with the capture plan's tag for that epoch (Step 12 fails with it). The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: a Phase D epoch relabelled Phase A on its seed record and its 100 rounds

Step 18 (Client-Seed Control & Phase D) takes the Phase D epochs from the capture plan in src/config.ts, not from the dataset's own tags: 400 rounds tagged D against 500 planned, and 100 rounds outside Phase D carrying a player-set seed. Steps 12 and 13 fail with it. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: stored verifier reply forged by one 2-dp tick, the settled round untouched

name: stored verifier request no longer the round it is filed under (nonce moved by one)

Step 25 (Production Verifier Parity & Result Cap) requires each stored verifier request to BE its round: the epoch's revealed seed, the round's client seed, nonce and target. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: one round's verifier reply deleted

name: production capture relabelled as another host
guard: The guard that fires is Step 21. Step 21 (Scope & Declared Limitations) must MEASURE the declared scope and not merely print it (G-SCOPE): the dataset header's host must be the host this suite declares, liqd.com. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: one epoch acquires an operator-sourced bet counter and 32 do not
guard: The guard that fires is Step 21. Step 21 (Scope & Declared Limitations) states limitation L2 (no operator bet counter was captured) as a measured property with one admissible value, 0 of 33 epochs; a counter on any epoch fails the step until the register is updated. Step 4 does not fail: the planted counter agrees with the observed last nonce. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: every epoch acquires an operator-sourced bet counter (limitation L2 stops being true)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 21. Step 21 (Scope & Declared Limitations) must FAIL when limitation L2 stops being true, so the published register cannot go stale under a passing run. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: every bet acquires a wallet balance record (limitation L3 stops being true)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 21. Step 21 (Scope & Declared Limitations) must FAIL when limitation L3 stops being true. The dataset is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the loader's hash check is not what catches it.

name: dataset edited and NOT re-pinned: the pin is the guard under test
guard: THE PIN IS THE GUARD UNDER TEST, so this entry names no step: no step runs. Every other dataset forgery in this file re-pins DATASET_SHA256 in the same edit, because a forger would and because otherwise the loader stops the run before anything is scored. That discipline is only honest if the pin is demonstrated somewhere, and this is where: one credit is changed with the pin left alone, and the expected outcome is `ERROR: dataset SHA-256 mismatch` with exit code 1, no verdict line and no step lines. It also fixes the scope of what a pin proves: that the file has not changed since it was pinned, and nothing about whether the file is the capture.

name: simulation artifact DELETED
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) must fail when outputs/simulation-results.json is absent: an artifact the report quotes must not be removable without a scored step noticing. Nothing in this entry re-pins; the pin is half of what is under test.

name: simulation convergence chart DELETED
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) must fail when outputs/rtp-convergence.html is absent: the chart is the twin output of the same producer run and is pinned.

name: simulation artifact present but UNREADABLE (the literal bytes `{not JSON`)
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) must fail on an artifact it could not read, with a named parse error; the SHA-256 comparison rejects it first and the parse arm is the second net.

name: simulation artifact replaced by a degenerate stub, pin left alone
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) must fail on a well-formed artifact that carries no statistics and no declared depths: the pin rejects it, and so does the shape and depth bind (pass1.draws, pass1.serial and a non-empty pass1.effectiveEdge[] must be present and agree with the SIM_* constants). What it does not establish is that the legacy Pass-1 numbers were measured (L9).

name: simulation artifact fabricated (perfect uniformity, zero serial correlation, a 5% PLAYER edge) and re-pinned
marker: THIS RUN DISAGREES WITH THE COMMITTED EVIDENCE
expect: every step at its baseline status and the verdict of record, but exit 1: the run disagrees with outputs/verification-results.json
guard: THIS ENTRY NAMES NO STEP BECAUSE NO STEP FAILS on the forged legacy Pass-1 figures: outputs/simulation-results.json is rewritten with a uniformity chi-squared of exactly 0, serial statistics of exactly 0 and an effective-edge band at an RTP of 1.05, every `pass` flag left true, and SIMULATION_SHA256 re-pinned in the same edit as a fabricating auditor would. What produces the non-zero exit is the run-vs-committed-artifact reproduction gate (fieldDiff, src/diff.ts, called in tests/verify.ts): Step 19's detail string carries the recomputed digest of the artifact, the forgery moves those bytes, and the string no longer matches the one in outputs/verification-results.json. That is a kill by BYTE IDENTITY, not by a step re-deriving the forged statistics, and a forger who also regenerates outputs/verification-results.json defeats it; `npm run simulate:check`, which regenerates the artifact from the recorded seed and requires it byte for byte, is what catches that. Limitation L9 states it.

name: a limits block the capture contradicts added to the dataset header
marker: THIS RUN DISAGREES WITH THE COMMITTED EVIDENCE
expect: every step at its baseline status and the verdict of record, but exit 1: the run disagrees with outputs/verification-results.json
guard: THIS ENTRY NAMES NO STEP BECAUSE NO STEP FAILS: the production dataset carries no meta.limits block, so one is added with values the settled rounds contradict, and the dataset is re-pinned. No scored step reads meta.limits; this audit establishes no casino limit at all (limitation L5), and the bounds the steps use are the capture plan's in src/config.ts, never a limit the artifact states about itself (G-BIND). What produces the non-zero exit is the reproduction gate (fieldDiff): re-pinning moves the dataset digest, which the run reports and Steps 12 and 19 print, so the run no longer matches outputs/verification-results.json. A kill by byte identity, declared as one.

name: Pass-1 grid prefix win count moved by one and re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 23. Step 23 (Simulation Pass 1) replays the stored prefixes from the recorded master seed on every run and requires them to reproduce.

name: Pass-1 grid: target 2x loses 4,000 wins and is re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 23. Step 23 (Simulation Pass 1) re-derives RTP convergence from the grid's integer win counts against the exact win probability, with a band of 5 standard deviations plus one count.

name: Pass-1 grid master seed rewritten and re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 23. Step 23 (Simulation Pass 1) binds the artifact's recorded master seed to PASS1_MASTER_SEED in src/config.ts.

name: Pass-1 grid acquires a generatedAt timestamp and is re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 23. Step 23 (Simulation Pass 1) rejects run metadata in an artifact of record.

name: Pass-1 grid: 500 counts moved between two histogram bins, totals kept, re-pinned
marker: THIS RUN DISAGREES WITH THE COMMITTED EVIDENCE
guard: NOT killed by a scored step: the re-derived chi-squared moves but stays well inside the bound and the prefix replay does not cover the body of the stream, so Step 23 PASSES. Killed by BYTE IDENTITY only: the run-vs-committed-artifact reproduction gate sees Step 23's detail (the digest and the chi-squared) differ from outputs/verification-results.json; and by `npm run pass1:check`, which replays all 11,000,000 draws and requires the regeneration to be byte-identical. Declared so the limit of the per-run prefix replay is on the record.

name: declared capture-retry nonce gap: epoch 5 nonce 25 removed and named in DECLARED_CAPTURE_GAPS
guard: The guard that fires is Step 4. Step 4 (Nonce Audit) must DISCLOSE a gap the capture log attributes to a retry as a FLAG with origin = capture (profile LIMBO-04), never fold it into a PASS. The population constants are untouched, so Step 12 also fails; the entry names Step 4 because its [FLAG] line is what is under test.

name: legacy simulation artifact: a p-value of 1.7 written in and re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) checks every numeric leaf of the pinned JSON artifacts against its declared value domain (src/domains.ts): a probability of 1.7 is outside [0, 1].

name: live-sample draws sorted into value order before the serial tests
replace:
draws.sort((x, y) => x - y);
  const n = draws.length;
guard: Step 22 (Live-Sample Fit) must be able to fire: sorted draws carry perfect serial dependence. The step is INFORMATIONAL by policy, so it reports [INFO] (reported, never counted, verdict unchanged) and no step FAILs or FLAGs; the run still exits 1 because Step 22's status and detail no longer match outputs/verification-results.json (the reproduction gate). Listed in this file and not in tests/mutations.json because the kill is an INFO status plus the reproduction gate, not a failing step.

name: reply record: a verifier reply's body forged (result one cent up), recorded digest left as received, record re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) recomputes the SHA-256 and byte length of every reply body the reply record keeps and requires them to be what the runner recorded for the bytes as received; the forged body no longer is. It also holds every verifier reply to the dataset's verifier field. The record is re-pinned in the same edit, as a forger would, so the pin is not what catches it. The builder rerun of Step 19 also finds the record is not what the exports make. No other step reads the verifier replies of the record.

name: reply record: the same forged verifier reply with its recorded byte length and SHA-256 recomputed to match, record re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 19. Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) holds every verifier reply in the reply record to the dataset's verifier field (request, echo, result, win flag, multiplier, Date): a forger who also rewrites the recorded digest still leaves a reply that is not the one in E01. The record is re-pinned in the same edit.

name: reply record: the client-seed rotation reply opening run 1's epoch 1 dated one second after the epoch's first bet, record re-pinned
guard: The guard that fires is Step 2. Step 2 (Next-Seed Pre-Commitment Chain) reads LIQD's Date headers in the reply record and requires, on every epoch, the reply that published the commitment, the rotation reply to the client-seed request and the first place-bet reply in that order; the moved Date puts the client seed after the first bet. The Date is outside the hashed body, so Step 19's digest check does not see it. The record is re-pinned in the same edit.

Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) recomputes each shipped runner build's id from its source (the first 12 hex of the SHA-256 of the source with the id removed from its version string) and requires the seed constructor with 6 bytes of crypto.getRandomValues: the edited source reproduces neither, although its file pin was moved to match.

Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) re-hashes every reply body in the shipped exports against the byte length and SHA-256 the runner recorded, and requires each export to be the file the dataset header names by SHA-256; the converter rerun then refuses the export too. The export's own pin is moved to match, so the pin is not what catches it.

Step 19 (Artifact Integrity) reruns the record builder on the shipped exports and requires the reply record byte for byte; the export still carries the digest the runner recorded, so the bent one is caught.
